title: Neuresthetics Genius Study belief-system record (YAML front matter of systems/<CODE>.md)
description: Field meanings: docs/DATA_DICTIONARY.md (Part 3). Coding rules: docs/CODING_GUIDE.md (Part 2).

record_type.description: Fixed: tells the validator which schema applies.

schema_version.description: Version of the schema this file was written against. Bump in the schema and in every file together. 1.1 (2026-10-01): descriptions updated for decisions P1, P5, S3, S4 and S5; no field or enum changes.

record_version.description: Integer, starts at 1. Add 1 every time the file's content changes in a commit.

review_status.description: Where the file is in review. Only a named human reviewer may set 'reviewed', with reviewed_by and reviewed_on (decision P5). Agents set only 'draft — unreviewed' or 'example — unreviewed' ('stub' for generated stubs). 'example — unreviewed' marks the worked examples.

collected_by.description: who ran the collection (person or agent)

collected_on.description: Date (YYYY-MM-DD) the first research run started.

last_updated.description: Date of the latest content change. Must match the newest change_log entry.

reviewed_by.description: Name of the human reviewer. Required when review_status is 'reviewed'.

reviewed_on.description: Date of the review. Required when review_status is 'reviewed'.

change_log.description: One entry per content change, oldest first: date, who, and a one-line summary.

record.description: Bookkeeping for this file: version, review state, who collected it, change history.

id.description: The v7.1 abbreviation code (e.g. PANT, CLASS_THEISM). Must equal the file name. One of the 77. The list is closed for v8 (decision S4): proposed new codes are collected in a list (code, why, example people, and for a split the people it would move) and added in one batch with one schema bump and Jason's approval.

v7_1_label.description: System name exactly as in the data book section 7 scoring note, or the section 6 score table (tables[4]) if the note has none. Never edited.

metaphysics.description: Core metaphysics. Each item: value (one to three sentences) plus a short stance label from the allowed list.

A_locus.description: A Locus: transcendent person outside the world (0) ... immanent in or identical with the world (4).

B_cause.description: B Cause: miracle, petition, reserved exemption (0) ... law, regularity, no special cases (4).

C_ledger.description: C Ledger: reward and punishment of persons (0) ... impersonal consequence, or none (4).

D_authority.description: D Authority: revelation outranks observation (0) ... observation and reason outrank revelation (4).

E_scope.description: E Scope: hidden exceptions for an in-group (0) ... same rules for stars, insects, humans (4). Scored on the world's order: the same rules for every kind of being and event, and no hidden in-group exceptions in this-world events (fortune, protection, answered petition, miracles for the favoured). Salvation, reward and punishment, and moral-community scope are scored on C_ledger, not here (decision P7, 2026-10-02).

lio_axes.description: Position on the five LIO axes (0-4 scale, decision P1), for the system's official or scholarly form. Variants that differ are described in schools_and_variants.

epistemology.description: How the system says knowledge is gained and checked.

ethics.description: Core ethical teaching, in one to three sentences.

ritual_and_practice.description: Required or typical practices (prayer, worship, meditation, none).

community_form.description: Organization: church, sangha, school, informal, none.

historical_stance.description: Stance on natural inquiry in the periods the roster covers.

current_stance.description: Stance today (official bodies or leading scholars).

science.description: Stance on natural science, historically and now.

schools_and_variants.description: Internal schools and forms, e.g. a scholarly and a popular form inside one tradition. Say which LIO axes move.

revised_rubric.description: Slot for revised scores (decision S3, 2026-10-01). Not started until the first coding pool is done and Jason opens it. Then: a cite for each axis score, two scorers score a sample independently and report agreement before the rest are scored, and Jason approves the final numbers. Revised scores sit beside v7_1_rubric and never overwrite it.

use_when.description: When to use the code. Where the v7.1 coding rules name the code, the rule is quoted verbatim.

do_not_use_when.description: Common mistakes and the code to use instead.

neighbors.description: Codes easily confused with this one.

coding_guidance.description: How to decide whether a person gets this code.

data_quality_flags.description: Plain statements of conflicts between sources, doubtful dates, or anything a reader should distrust.

open_questions.description: Questions this run could not settle, phrased so the next run can act on them.

review.description: Data quality notes and open questions for the reviewer.

sources.description: Every source cited in this file. Ids are S1, S2, ... and are local to the file. Every source must be cited somewhere, and every citation must point here.

sentinel.description: TODO = not researched yet. UNKNOWN = researched, no reliable source gives it (say what was checked in how_known). BELOW_THRESHOLD = some evidence, but under certainty 0.5, so the value is withheld (describe the evidence in note).

certainty.description: See docs/CODING_GUIDE.md. Worldview claims: 1.0 written profession, 0.7 consistent private letters, 0.5 scholarly reconstruction. Other facts: 1.0 established, 0.7 probable, 0.5 contested. Below 0.5: withhold the value (BELOW_THRESHOLD).

source.description: id of an entry in the sources list

locator.description: page, folio, section, letter number, paragraph, or URL anchor

note.description: Why it differs, or why it was not preferred.

alternative.description: A competing value from another source, with its citation.

claimRules.description: A filled value needs certainty, at least one citation and a how_known note. UNKNOWN / BELOW_THRESHOLD need how_known. TODO needs nothing.

basis.description: Evidence basis for a worldview claim. Sets the certainty ceiling: written_profession 1.0, consistent_private_letters 0.7, scholarly_reconstruction 0.5. Certainty may sit below the ceiling (e.g. at most 0.7 when the record names a plausible alternative score; CODING_GUIDE §3), never above it.

lioScore.description: 0-4 ordinal scale (decision P1, 2026-10-01): 0 interventionist pole, 1 leans interventionist, 2 mixed, 3 leans LIO, 4 LIO pole. Certainty is recorded separately.

relation.description: Read as: '<code> is <relation> this system'. E.g. in PANT.md, {code: STOIC, relation: 'parent tradition'} means Stoicism is a parent tradition of PANT. CLTHEI and CLASS_THEISM are 'neighbor (easily confused)' to each other (decision S5).
